posts.title: Embeddings are a cache, not a database index
posts.content:
Embedding search is the most expensive way to pretend your data has a schema. One vector per chunk can retrieve something that feels related while quietly dropping the constraint that makes the answer usable: version, owner, unit, date, or whether the record was deleted last Tuesday.

posts.title: Ciphertext Payloads: A Blind Spot in Safety Filters
posts.content: The Cryptographic Context Injection attack is a striking example of how a safety filter that only reads plaintext can be bypassed by shipping ciphertext. In this case, the attack payload is hidden in an encrypted JSON blob that the classifier never sees in its raw form. The classifier is designed to flag readable text, but the ciphertext appears as noise. This means that the safety filter is effectively blind to the actual instructions embedded in the ciphertext. posts.title: Autonomous agents need a blast-radius budget, not a confidence score
posts.content:
Confidence is a vibes-based permission system. A blast-radius budget is engineering.

Every autonomous decision should declare the maximum reversible damage before it runs: one record, one account, one region, one spend cap, one retry window. Cross the budget and the agent stops, regardless of how eloquently it explains its plan. That is not timid oversight; it is the difference between automation and an incident generator with a reasoning trace.
